1.instr: You will hear three different extracts. For each question, choose the correct answer. There are two questions for each extract.

extracts.intro: You hear a trainee teacher called Susanna talking to her tutor.

1.stem: What point does the tutor make about a teacher's attitude?
options: A good teacher can put any subject across effectively.
Students will pick up on a teacher's commitment.
There's little point in a teacher trying to fake passion for a subject.
complaining about her students' lack of enthusiasm
proposing ways of making her subject more appealing
asking for ideas about exercises her students could do

extracts.intro: You hear a student called Sam telling his friend Ella about a concert he's been to.

options: suggest how the visual impact could have been improved.
challenge Ella's preconceptions about the music.
persuade Ella to go to a similar one in the future.

4.stem: In Sam's opinion, what makes the performer stand out?
options: the influence her academic background has on her music
the instinctive way she responds to her audience
the high level of stage presence she displays

extracts.intro: You hear a woman telling her friend about new policies adopted by her company.

5.stem: Staff have been planting trees in order to
options: promote a desirable image.
encourage a spirit of mutual co-operation.
compensate for environmental damage.

6.stem: The company was surprised that its remote working initiative resulted in
options: more appreciative customers.
a better standard of new recruits.
a more motivated workforce.

2.instr: You will hear a scientist called Jim Weller giving a talk about some robots he has created and how they function like insects called termites. For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write a word or short phrase.
2.title: Robots Like Termites

Jim uses the word [[8]] to refer to the group of robots he's created to function as independent units.
Jim observed termites depositing partially consumed [[9]] in shared habitats, which activated a response from other termites.

3.instr: You will hear an interview in which a historian called Mark Connor and a writer called Judith Monroe are talking about the history of the underground railway in London. For each question, choose the correct answer.

15.stem: Mark says that the problems which led to the creation of the railway
options: resulted from poor urban planning.
were similar to those we have today.
typified the thinking of their age.
only had one possible solution.

16.stem: Judith believes that the engineering methods used to make the first tunnel
options: worked surprisingly quickly.
were too basic to be efficient.
caused a minimum amount of disruption.
resulted in the loss of too many homes.

17.stem: How does Mark feel about the public reaction when the first underground line opened?
options: disappointed by their reluctance to go underground
struck by their willingness to tolerate lengthy journeys
amused by their unfounded fears
impressed by their general enthusiasm

18.stem: Judith and Mark both say that, during the early years of its construction, the railway
options: created many jobs for people.
had a big influence on urban development.
inspired imitators all over the world.
made national heroes of its developers.

19.stem: Judith compares certain underground stations to a classic film in that
options: they are designed in the style of a particular era.
they give a feeling of being in a cinema.
they are a product of the same creative vision.
they give a similar sense of size and excitement.

20.stem: What does Mark think about the railway map?
options: It has come to represent the city.
It can confuse people unfamiliar with its format.
It encourages people to use the underground.
It is well designed for something so inexpensive.

4.instr: You will hear five short extracts in which people are talking about visits they have made to museums. For Task 1, choose from the list each speaker's reason for visiting the museum. For Task 2, choose from the list what impressed each speaker most about the museum. For each question, choose the correct answer. Complete both tasks.

tasks.label: Task 1
tasks.instr: choose from the list each speaker's reason for visiting the museum.

options.D: to follow up on a recommendation

tasks.label: Task 2
tasks.instr: choose from the list what impressed each speaker most about the museum.

options.E: the diversity of the items on show
